Container.Name: Unraid-Reverse-Proxy
Container.Overview:
Give every Docker container on your server a friendly name.
Map 192.168.1.50:8080 to openwebui.local, 192.168.1.50:8989 to sonarr.local, and so on. The container runs a reverse proxy that routes by hostname and an mDNS responder that makes those .local names resolve across your LAN — no router, Pi-hole or hosts-file changes needed on any client. Other suffixes (home.arpa, internal, lan) work too, and every service can answer on several at once.
It also serves a launch screen listing every mapped service with live up/down indicators, collapsible categories, drag-to-arrange ordering and configurable appearance, plus a password-protected admin panel. Icons can be picked from the Community Applications catalogue or uploaded.
SETUP — PLEASE READ, TWO STEPS:
1. Give this container its OWN IP ADDRESS. Set Network Type to "Custom: br0" and enter a Fixed IP outside your DHCP pool. The Unraid webGUI already owns port 80 on the host, and mDNS needs real multicast, so the default bridge network will not work.
2. Attach a second network ONCE, after the first start, by running this in a terminal:
docker network connect bridge unraid-reverse-proxy
Unraid's template can only set one network, and br0 is an ipvlan network — a container on it cannot reach its own host, so without this second connection every service you map shows as offline. The app detects this and says so in its log and on the System tab if you forget.
First run: browse to the IP you assigned and create your login. Nothing is preconfigured and there is no default password.
Container.Description: Reverse proxy plus mDNS responder that maps your Docker containers to .local hostnames, with a dashboard and admin UI. Requires its own IP on br0.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Stores config.json — your routes, settings, cached icons and login.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: Port the proxy and web UI listen on. Leave at 80 so your URLs stay clean; the container has its own IP, so nothing else is using it.

Config.Name: mDNS Port
Config.Description: Multicast DNS. Leave at 5353 — clients will not find .local names on any other port.

Config.Name: HTTP_PORT
Config.Description: Must match the HTTP Port above.
